partners.diseaseBName: methylmalonic aciduria and homocystinuria type cblC
partners.mechanism_chain: NCF4 (HGNC:7713) —DISRUPTS→ Oxidative Stress Response Pathway; Oxidative Stress Response Pathway —DECREASES→ Cobalamin-dependent enzymes; Cobalamin-dependent enzymes —DISRUPTS→ Homocysteine accumulation; Cobalamin-dependent enzymes —DISRUPTS→ Methylmalonic acid accumulation; MMACHC (HGNC:7445) —DISRUPTS→ Cobalamin Metabolism; Cobalamin Metabolism —DISRUPTS→ Homocysteine accumulation; Cobalamin Metabolism —DISRUPTS→ Methylmalonic acid accumulation; Homocysteine accumulation —LEADS_TO→ Elevated homocysteine (HP:0001349); Methylmalonic acid accumulation —LEADS_TO→ Elevated methylmalonic acid (HP:0003118). Loss-of-function mutations in NCF4 lead to dysregulation of the oxidative stress response, which in turn impairs the function of cobalamin-dependent enzymes. This impairment disrupts the normal metabolism of homocysteine and methylmalonic acid. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in MMACHC directly disrupt cobalamin metabolism, leading to the accumulation of homocysteine and methylmalonic acid. Both pathways converge on the accumulation of these metabolites, causing the respective phenotypes.

partners.diseaseBName: X-linked Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases due to CYBB deficiency
partners.mechanism_chain: NCF4 (HGNC:18302) —BINDS→ NADPH oxidase complex (GO:0005914); CYBB (HGNC:2402) —BINDS→ NADPH oxidase complex (GO:0005914); NCF4 (HGNC:18302) —DISRUPTS→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) production; CYBB (HGNC:2402) —DISRUPTS→ Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) production; Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) production —LEADS_TO→ Impaired bacterial killing (HP:0002719); Reactive Oxygen Species (ROS) production —LEADS_TO→ Increased susceptibility to mycobacteria (HP:0002719). Loss-of-function mutations in NCF4 (causing MONDO:0013507) and CYBB (causing X-linked Mendelian susceptibility to mycobacterial diseases) both impair the assembly and function of the NADPH oxidase complex. This complex is essential for producing reactive oxygen species (ROS) to kill phagocytosed bacteria. Consequently, defects in either NCF4 or CYBB lead to impaired bacterial killing and increased susceptibility to infections, particularly mycobacterial infections.

partners.mechanism_chain: NCF4 (HGNC:7722) —DISRUPTS→ NADPH oxidase activity (GO:0004601); NADPH oxidase activity (GO:0004601) —DECREASES→ Reactive oxygen species (CHEBI:17666); Reactive oxygen species (CHEBI:17666) —LEADS_TO→ Neutrophil dysfunction (HP:0003217); CD36 (HGNC:2217) —DISRUPTS→ Phagocytosis (GO:0006909); Phagocytosis (GO:0006909) —DECREASES→ Platelet aggregation (HP:0011301); Platelet aggregation (HP:0011301) —LEADS_TO→ Bleeding tendency (HP:0001892); Reactive oxygen species (CHEBI:17666) —DISRUPTS→ Phagocytosis (GO:0006909). Loss-of-function mutations in NCF4 disrupt NADPH oxidase activity, leading to decreased reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, which contributes to neutrophil dysfunction. Simultaneously, loss-of-function mutations in CD36 disrupt phagocytosis, leading to decreased platelet aggregation and ultimately a bleeding tendency. The convergence occurs at the level of ROS, where decreased ROS production can impair various cellular functions, including aspects of phagocytosis and immune cell function, potentially exacerbating platelet dysfunction and bleeding.
